Help

        

        
        

          

          
Piper restores your last open file, applied edits and Undo/Redo history after a refresh. Download to save a file on disk; your original stays unchanged. Unfinished form entries reset on refresh.

          
    
            
  • Download Preset: the selected preset as MHP; excludes device settings and tuning tables.
    • 
            
  • Download Everything: all eight presets, device settings and tuning tables as MHD.
    • 
            
  • Download JSON: the entire open file as JSON.
    • 
          

          
Download Everything saves an opened or newly created MHD setup.

        

        

        

          

          
New setup in the top bar creates eight preset slots. With a standalone preset open, choose its destination slot or an empty setup in Presets.

          
Inside a setup, New preset clears only the chosen slot. Copy preset copies from another slot or file into the destination you choose. Undo restores replaced slots.

          
Device settings edits the setup’s shared settings, default port names and tuning slots. These changes are included in Download Everything and Download JSON; Download Preset does not include them.

        

        

        

          

          
To convert edited JSON back to a Midihub file, load it with Open file. Choose Download Everything for MHD or Download Preset for MHP.

        

        

        

          

          
Hover over a pipe for a temporary editor; click to keep it open. Escape or clicking empty map space closes it.

          
Press Delete to remove the selected pipe. On the pipeline’s starting input, Delete removes the whole pipeline. Undo restores either.

          
Enter notes as numbers or names: 60 or C4.

          
Choose Add mapping in the form before selecting another pipe; otherwise the unfinished mapping is discarded.

          
Dropping a processing pipe on empty space creates a pipeline with a MIDI A Input.

        

        

        

          

          
Drag empty map space to pan. Scroll to zoom at the pointer.

          
Drag a menu by its dotted grip into any of the four map corners. The outline and message show where it will land. Drop above another menu to insert it there, or below the last menu to append it. You can also click the grip and then click the destination. Escape cancels the move.

          
With the grip focused, press Left or Right to change sides, Shift+Up or Shift+Down to switch between the top and bottom, or Up or Down to reorder menus in the same corner. Home restores the default position.

          
Drag the solid grip on the inward edge to change a menu’s width. Double-click the grip or focus it and press Delete to restore the default width. MIDI activity grows with the log and scrolls when it fills the available space. Drag its bottom grip to set a height or reset it to return to automatic sizing.

        

        

        

          

          
Choose MIDI Studio in the bottom bar to open the tray. Beside it, you can start or stop all playback and adjust master volume. Selecting an input on the map opens its tab and traces its route. The centered tray fits its widest configured tab and the tallest tab at that width. Drag its top edge or use the Up and Down arrows on the handle to choose a height. Closing the tray or switching tabs keeps playback running. Hover over an input tab for its physical port.

          
Choose an input tab, then use Add source to send MIDI to that input. With Notes, choose a chord or arpeggio under Play as. Use MIDI message to send one event. To reassign a source, choose Move… or drag its tab onto another input box on the map.

          
For a real keyboard or controller, add MIDI input, allow browser MIDI access and choose a MIDI device. On Windows, Chrome and Microsoft Edge can receive notes from your device when you open Piper directly from disk. Notes and controls keep their original channels. Incoming clock and transport reach the same Piper input. Use Disconnect to stop listening. Piper remembers the device for your next session.

          
For Notes and MIDI input, use Destination to choose a General MIDI sound or an external output. For MIDI message and Expression pedal, use MIDI out or leave it at Piper only. Choose Find MIDI outputs…, allow access, then select your synth’s port. It receives the messages from that source that reach a preset output, with the preset’s pitch, channel and controller changes applied. To send SysEx, choose SysEx on a MIDI message source and press Send. Allow the separate browser permission for system exclusive messages when prompted.

          
Add an Expression pedal and choose its input, channel and CC. Its floating control stays on the map when the tray closes. Unpin keeps the pedal in its input tab. Each pedal retains its physical position across preset changes. Jump sends the new position on movement. Pickup waits until you reach or cross the reference value. Value scaling moves the output gradually from that reference.

          
Each Notes source has a Hold checkbox. Leave it off for a half-second chord or one pass through an arpeggio. Turn it on to sustain the chord or repeat the arpeggio until you stop playback. The source’s play button, Start input and Start all use that setting. Stop the source, its input or all playback to release its notes. To test a mapping, hold a chord and move the floating pedal. MIDI activity reports each mapping and its value.

          
Open Clock & transport to set tempo, choose what starts with playback, or send clock and transport independently. Clock and MIDI Start are included by default on each input. Stop all ends the session and releases tracked notes. If a synth keeps sounding, press MIDI Panic in the footer. It silences browser playback and sends All Sound Off, pedal releases and All Notes Off on every channel of each selected MIDI output. It works with the tray closed and while playback is idle.

          
For General MIDI sounds, adjust Volume on the source or use the slider beside Start all for the whole browser mix. Set the listening level of an external synth on the synth itself. It receives the preset’s MIDI velocities and CC values at any master volume.

          
In MIDI activity, Log messages chooses the messages shown and copied. Animated chooses the messages that light up the map. Both start with every message except clock ticks. Each wire lights when its source or pipe sends a message. A filter’s outgoing wire shows only what passed. Under Animated, Spark speed controls how fast the light moves along each wire. Choose Static to mark arrivals in place. Piper also uses static feedback when your system requests reduced motion.

          
The footer identifies sounding sources even with the tray closed. Open MIDI activity to see their pitches and routes. Last heard shows the most recent notes after release.

          
Scroll up to review earlier MIDI events or scroll to the bottom to follow live activity. Changing Log messages filters the whole recorded history. Copy to clipboard copies the matching entries with their original numbers and mapping details. Clear log starts a new history at 1.

          
Each pipe shows its settings while idle and its result when active. The left edge flashes on received or generated MIDI. A pulse of light travels from the pipeline number to the first pipe and between pipes as MIDI reaches them. A filtered message stops at the filter. Active CC LFOs show the current value and eight seconds of output on the same time scale. Stop all and MIDI Panic return the cards to their settings. Their final Note Off and transport Stop messages animate on the wires they traverse when those messages are selected under Animated. Panic reports direct hardware resets in the footer. To review a pipe’s last messages and counts, open Pipe activity in its inspector.

          
Simulation details identifies settings and routing combinations that prevent output playback. For example, Micro Scale needs its tuning definition in the open setup. The activity log still shows incoming events.

          
This browser remembers your sources, instruments, MIDI ports and levels. Playback starts when you use a play or send control.

          
Synthesis adapted from the supplied Harmonic Studio. General MIDI voices use WebAudioTinySynth under Apache-2.0.

        

        

        

          

          
The map places hardware inputs toward the top left and hardware outputs toward the bottom right. This arrangement does not change the saved pipeline order.

          
Apply pipeline order saves the arrangement and renumbers the pipelines.

        

        

        

          

          
Open the file you want to copy into. In Presets, choose Another file as the source, select the source and destination presets, then Replace preset. Only that destination preset is replaced.
